title: Decomposing A Neural Learner
abstract: arXiv:2610.14388v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Neural learners for classification and regression are often criticized as black boxes. We propose a probabilistic decomposition of neural learners that accounts for heterogeneous predictability across the feature space. A training procedure combining the EM algorithm, stochastic gradient descent, and maximum likelihood estimation is developed to jointly learn the predictable component and an input-dependent reliability score. We show that the optimal decomposed learner recovers the response distribution within the predictable component, while the reliability score characterizes the predictability of individual observations. We further extend the framework to incorporate localized feature transformations. Experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

translated_abstract: 用于分类和回归的神经学习器常被批评为黑箱。我们提出了一种神经学习器的概率分解方法，该方法考虑了特征空间中不同区域可预测性的异质性。我们开发了一种结合EM算法、随机梯度下降和最大似然估计的训练过程，用于联合学习可预测分量和依赖于输入的可靠性分数。我们证明最优的分解学习器能够恢复可预测分量内的响应分布，同时可靠性分数刻画了单个观测值的可预测性。我们进一步扩展了该框架以纳入局部化特征变换。在合成数据集和真实数据集上的实验证明了所提框架的有效性。
tldr: 提出一种神经学习器的概率分解框架，将模型分解为可预测分量和输入相关的可靠性分数，以应对特征空间中可预测性的异质性，从而提升神经网络的透明度与可解释性。
en_tdlr: A probabilistic decomposition framework that splits neural learners into a predictable component and an input-dependent reliability score, addressing heterogeneous predictability across the feature space and enhancing transparency and interpretability.
